author_declaration: 40 vulnerability examples authored for Stage 7M. None reproduces the surface wording, variable names, framework, or sink identifier of any v0 / v1 / v2 / v2.1(g4) / Stage 7K / Stage 7L snippet. CWE-89 and CWE-78 pools were constructed to EMPHASIZE their disambiguating context (database driver vs OS shell) because those are the two categories under test. Prompts / catalogs / sampler / seeds / scoring were frozen BEFORE any of these snippets were evaluated. No model output for these 40 snippets has been inspected prior to the recorded run.

distinctness_vs_prior.cwe_89_strategy: Each CWE-89 snippet names a database driver OR surfaces SQL keywords (SELECT/UPDATE/WHERE/JOIN) plainly in the code. Four distinct driver families: psycopg2, mysql2, sqlx, ActiveRecord.
distinctness_vs_prior.cwe_78_strategy: Each CWE-78 snippet uses an unambiguous OS-command sink: shell=True, os.popen, pipes.quote inversion, Deno.Command, child_process.spawn with array-less shell string.

snippets.code: cur = conn.cursor(); cur.execute('SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = \'%s\'' % email)
snippets.desc: psycopg2 cursor runs a SELECT with user email interpolated by % formatting; no bound parameter.

snippets.code: const [rows] = await mysql2.query(`UPDATE sessions SET last_seen=NOW() WHERE token=${token}`);
snippets.desc: mysql2 driver receives a template-literal UPDATE statement that interpolates a session token string.

snippets.code: sqlx::query(&format!("SELECT * FROM audit WHERE actor_id = {}", actor_id)).fetch_all(&pool).await
snippets.desc: sqlx::query receives a format! SQL string with actor_id (string) spliced into a WHERE clause.
ActiveRecord where() receives an interpolated string instead of a parameterized hash.
Flask handler spawns ffmpeg via a shell with the request-supplied src path inside an f-string.
Node spawn is handed /bin/sh -c and a template literal interpolating a query parameter.
exec.Command invokes bash -c with a concatenated tar command and user-provided archive path.
Deno.Command runs sh -c with a template literal interpolating the host query parameter.
Angular template binds [innerHTML] with a custom pipe that turns off DomSanitizer; review.body is user-controlled.
Django view interpolates a GET parameter into inline JavaScript without JS-context escaping.
Express path parameter embedded in HTML directly via template literal.
Mustache triple-stash renders raw HTML from a user comment variable without escaping.
Go handler joins /srv/invoices with a query parameter and reads the resulting file.
ASP.NET controller returns bytes from a filesystem path built with Path.Combine and a request query value.
Python tarfile.extractall on an uploaded archive; no member name sanitization; slip into /opt/incoming parent paths.
Java servlet opens a FileInputStream by concatenating /var/exports with a request parameter.
PyJWT decode with signature verification and expiration check both disabled.
jsonwebtoken.verify allows both HS256 and RS256 with the same key material, enabling alg confusion.
Go jwt.Parse error is discarded; the resulting token.Valid field is never checked before using claims.

snippets.code: DecodedJWT dj = JWT.decode(token); User u = userRepo.findById(dj.getSubject());
snippets.desc: java-jwt JWT.decode() parses but does not verify; sub claim read directly.

snippets.code: file, h, _ := r.FormFile("f"); dst, _ := os.Create("/var/www/public/" + h.Filename); io.Copy(dst, file)
snippets.desc: Go handler copies an uploaded file into /var/www/public using the client-supplied filename.

snippets.code: await using var fs = System.IO.File.Create(Path.Combine("wwwroot", file.FileName)); await file.CopyToAsync(fs);
snippets.desc: ASP.NET Core writes an IFormFile to wwwroot keyed by the client-supplied FileName; no extension or MIME check.
Rails action writes an uploaded file into public/u using params[:f].original_filename directly.
Django view extracts an uploaded zip under /opt/plugins with no entry-name validation.

snippets.code: db.Exec("INSERT INTO users(email, password) VALUES (?, ?)", email, password)
snippets.desc: Go handler inserts the submitted password column as plaintext with no hashing or encryption step.
Node handler emits the auth cookie without Secure or HttpOnly flags.

snippets.code: logger.info("card={} cvv={} exp={}", cardNumber, cvv, expiry);
snippets.desc: Payment service logs the raw PAN, CVV, and expiry to the standard application log.
Session cache stores a bearer token string in plaintext under a predictable key.
Account-deletion form posts without any CSRF token; session cookie is the only check.

snippets.code: @app.get('/pay'); def pay(to, amount): return gateway.transfer(session.user, to, amount)
snippets.desc: FastAPI GET endpoint triggers a money transfer; no origin / token check; vulnerable via .
Fastify POST changes email based on cookie-identified session; no CSRF or Origin check.

snippets.code: class LogsController < ApplicationController; skip_before_action :verify_authenticity_token; def destroy; Log.destroy(params[:id]); end; end
snippets.desc: Rails controller disables CSRF protection on a destroy action.
Flask admin gate is a plain compare on a client-controlled custom header.
Express marks a request internal when X-Forwarded-For prefix is 10. (easily spoofed).
Servlet checks substring of the Referer header to authorize a transfer action.
Go middleware trusts the Sec-Fetch-Site request header for cross-origin decisions.

snippets.code: import hashlib; token = hashlib.new('md4', secret + nonce).hexdigest()
snippets.desc: Token derivation uses MD4 (broken) over secret + nonce concatenation.

snippets.code: Cipher c = Cipher.getInstance("Blowfish"); c.init(ENC, new SecretKeySpec(k, "Blowfish"));
snippets.desc: Blowfish (64-bit block) used for bulk encryption; insecure at modern data volumes.
Node crypto.createCipher uses 3DES with a password (not a KDF-derived key).
Go handler uses RC4 with a hard-coded key for payload encryption.
